title: Top categories by monthly paid gross revenue
brief: Rank monthly category revenue while preserving qualifying ties.
instructions: Return UTC 2024 paid gross transaction revenue by month and category identity, with category name and competition rank.
Use the half-open interval from 2024-01-01 00:00:00 UTC through, but not including, 2025-01-01 00:00:00 UTC.
Rank revenue descending within each month and retain every competition rank at most three, including all cutoff ties.
Use transaction quantity times transaction price, not catalog price. Months and categories without qualifying items are absent.
Sort month then rank ascending; ordering within equal month/rank peers is free.
starterSql:
SELECT
  CAST(date_trunc('month', o.ordered_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS DATE) AS mon,
  c.category_id,
  c.c_name,
  CAST(sum(CAST(i.qty AS DECIMAL(18,0)) * i.unit_price) AS DECIMAL(38,2)) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
  AND o.ordered_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00'
  AND o.ordered_at < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-01-01 00:00:00+00'
GROUP BY mon, c.category_id, c.c_name
ORDER BY mon, revenue DESC, c.category_id;
starterExplanation: This valid starter computes monthly totals. Add competition ranking and the rank cutoff to solve the challenge.

hints.text: RANK gives equal revenues the same rank and leaves gaps afterward. DENSE_RANK does not leave those gaps.
Use the monthly totals as a CTE. Apply RANK with PARTITION BY mon and ORDER BY revenue DESC. Filter ranks in an outer query.
Keep every rank-three tie. Do not include category_id in the window ordering. Sort the final result by mon and rnk. January has four qualifying rows.
